attempts.summary: Established an AIDE-based file-integrity baseline for /etc on node1 (RHEL 9.8): installed aide, scoped /etc/aide.conf to /etc (disabled non-etc top-level trees /boot,/bin,/sbin,/lib,/lib64,/opt,/usr,/root), and strengthened the catch-all /etc rule from PERMS to NORMAL to add content hashing, since the stock PERMS-only rule silently missed content-only edits to files without an explicit rule (proven via an /etc/motd test). Initialized the AIDE database (1131 entries), verified a clean check, verified detection of a deliberate content change, then reverted the test change and re-verified clean. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured boot_id and AIDE db checksum pre-restart, issued a detached systemctl reboot so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until node1 was reachable again, confirmed boot_id changed (bf4e9cbb-84f9-45f0-9b81-6602b98cea07 -> 4e4bd6a3-e34e-42dd-8fc8-71d0a915e4ad), and confirmed the AIDE config, database checksum, and a fresh aide --check all show the baseline intact and clean post-restart.
